thesis: Linde reported confirmed Q3 2026 results on Oct 29: record sales of $9.4B (+9%), adjusted EPS of $4.59 (+9%), and operating cash flow of $3.2B (+8%). It guided full-year adjusted EPS to $17.82-17.92 (+8-9%), and commentary points to a tailwind from AI chip fab demand. This suggests the 60-day gain rests on steady execution, though the move began before the report and the sources do not show which factor drove most of it. Reported EPS fell 11% on a jump in restructuring charges. The Russia/Amur dispute remains open: Linde won a Stockholm arbitration award on Oct 15, 2026 that bars Gazprom from enforcing its roughly 85.7B-ruble Russian judgment, but Gazprom may challenge it, and the contingent liability is about $0.7B. No hearing or ruling date is scheduled within 90 days.
invalidation: Revisit if Linde cuts full-year adjusted EPS guidance, if restructuring charges keep growing, or if Gazprom successfully challenges the SCC award and moves to enforce the Russian judgment.

thesis: Home Depot's 60-day gain is concentrated in a sector-wide housing rally after the midterms (+6.5% on Nov 4 and about 12% in a week, alongside Lowe's and homebuilders), a bet on future affordability policy and lower mortgage rates that has not happened yet. The 10-year yield barely moved (about 4.9%), existing home sales ran at a 3.99M annual pace in September (down 2.2% year over year), and analysts expect only about 2% normalized EPS growth this year, which suggests the move is ahead of the fundamentals. Q3 earnings on Nov 17 are a binary test of whether any of it is reaching the stores. No scheduled litigation or governance events turned up in this run's searches.
invalidation: Revisit the avoid if the Nov 17 Q3 report shows comps turning positive with guidance raised, or if the housing policy or mortgage-rate relief the rally is pricing in actually materializes.

thesis: Costco's 16% climb over 60 days to near its 52-week high is backed by a company-disclosed October sales report: net sales of $24.50B (+12.6%), total comps of +11.1%, U.S. comps of +12.6%, and digital sales up 22.5%. This suggests steady share gains and membership-driven traffic. The strongest counter-evidence is that gasoline prices and FX inflate the headline comps. Even so, comps excluding both were still +7.3% company-wide and +8.1% in the U.S., so the read holds without those tailwinds. The tariff-refund suit is one Costco filed against the government at the Court of International Trade, not a case against Costco; refunds are already flowing and management says it will reinvest them in member value. No restatement or governance event turned up.
invalidation: Revisit if November monthly comps (due early December) slow sharply, especially U.S. comps excluding gas and FX below roughly mid-single digits, or if Q1 FY27 earnings show membership renewal or margin deterioration.

thesis: P&G's fiscal Q1 FY27 report (Oct 22) showed 4% organic sales growth driven by volume, core EPS up 1%, maintained organic sales/EPS guidance, and raised all-in sales guidance to reflect the Thorne acquisition that closed Oct 1; shares reportedly rose about 3.3% on the print. This suggests the 60-day climb to near its 52-week high rests partly on a confirmed volume-led quarter. However, reported gross margin fell 160bp and management flagged rising commodity, energy and freight costs weighing on Q2 and the second half. The rally also coincided with a broad selloff in chip and AI stocks since early October, so defensive rotation may be a second contributor, and this research cannot say which factor dominates. No scheduled litigation milestone or governance event turned up.
invalidation: A guidance cut in organic sales or EPS, or Q2 margins falling enough from cost inflation to put the FY27 EPS outlook in doubt

thesis: Lilly's Q3 2026 report (Oct 29) showed revenue up 39% to $24.4B, driven by Mounjaro and Zepbound, and adjusted EPS of $7.48 against a ~$5.38 consensus. It also raised full-year guidance, and the oral GLP-1 Foundayo (orforglipron) nearly doubled sequentially to $184M. This suggests the 60-day advance to near its 52-week high is backed by a confirmed, company-disclosed earnings beat. The strongest counter-evidence is that one-time items, including $410M of Jardiance milestones and favorable rebate-estimate adjustments, inflated the quarter; even excluding the $410M milestone, revenue would still have grown about 37%, so the core incretin demand read does not change. The FDA biologic-classification dispute over retatrutide and the copycat/compounder suits are open matters, but no ruling or deadline within ~90 days was found; tirzepatide product-liability bellwethers are reported only by a low-authority source as 'potentially late 2026 or early 2027', with no court-confirmed date. Next earnings are expected around early February 2027.
invalidation: Evidence that underlying Mounjaro/Zepbound demand is slowing once one-time items are stripped out, a guidance cut, or a court-confirmed near-term trial or ruling date (e.g. tirzepatide bellwether or retatrutide classification) that could reverse the read

thesis: Visa's fiscal Q4 2026 report (Oct 27) showed net revenue of $12.1B, non-GAAP EPS of $3.48 (+17% YoY), 10% constant-dollar payments volume growth, 14% cross-border growth, and a 16% dividend increase. This suggests the 60-day gain rests on a confirmed, steady fundamental print. Coverage of the reaction conflicts: Zacks calls it a beat, while Quiver Quantitative reports a slight miss and a lower stock afterward. The strongest bearish counterweight is legal and pricing pressure: the DOJ debit monopolization case has no trial date and looks likely to reach trial around 2028, and the revised $38B merchant swipe-fee settlement, which cuts fees, was found likely to get final approval by Judge Cogan, though the NRF plans further challenges. No hearing date within ~90 days was confirmed, and no governance event was found.
invalidation: A court-set hearing or ruling date in the DOJ or interchange litigation inside ~90 days, a slowdown in cross-border/payments volume growth, or the swipe-fee settlement being rejected

thesis: Micron's ~12% gain today came in a sector-wide memory and AI-chip rally after CoreWeave's Q3 results (revenue $3.66B, raised 2026 guidance) eased worries about AI infrastructure demand, and Morgan Stanley argued the valuation pullback improves memory stocks' risk-reward. This suggests today's bounce is sentiment-driven and sector-wide rather than tied to new Micron-specific disclosure. It follows a ~21.5% 60-day decline in which chip and memory stocks lost about $3.7T in value from Oct. 6. Possible positives include the reported capacity to repurchase more than 40% of shares by 2028 and an ongoing memory-pricing boom; against that, Micron's fiscal Q1 report is expected around mid-to-late December, a pending binary event. The Netlist patent dispute ($445M verdict upheld in 2025, plus newer DDR5 suits) is ongoing, but no scheduled step within ~90 days was found, and no restatement, for-cause auditor change or executive indictment was found.
invalidation: A company-specific confirmation, such as a fiscal Q1 beat with raised guidance or HBM pricing/contract disclosures, together with a sustained recovery of the 60-day downtrend

thesis: SK hynix's US ADS rose ~9.4-9.8% today in the same CoreWeave-driven memory rally, which suggests the bounce is sector-wide sentiment rather than new company-specific disclosure. It follows a ~26% 60-day decline that leaves the ADS below its July offering price of $149; that offering raised about $26.5B through 177.9M ADSs roughly 4 months ago, just outside the ~90-day dilution window. A company-specific positive is the ~40 trillion won (~$29B) buyback-and-cancel program running through Nov. 19, but it has not prevented the slide. Separately, Korean prosecutors indicted several former SK hynix employees in 2024-2025 for leaking company technology to Huawei/HiSilicon; read literally, that meets the governance_history criterion, although the company was the victim. No scheduled litigation milestone within ~90 days was found.
invalidation: A company-specific catalyst (earnings beat, HBM contract disclosure) plus a sustained recovery above the $149 ADS offering price

thesis: Marvell's 60-day drawdown is mostly the market's reaction to its Nov 2 agreement to buy Lumentum in a $115B all-stock deal. Marvell holders would own about 67% of the combined company, and the deal needs shareholder votes and a regulatory review expected to run into 1H 2028. The stock fell about 28% that week amid analyst downgrades over dilution. Today's +9% rebound tracked CoreWeave's results lifting AI connectivity names generally, which suggests sentiment rather than new Marvell-specific fundamentals. Management has again raised its FY2027/FY2028 revenue outlook and preliminary Q3 revenue held the guidance midpoint, so the core data-center business looks intact; fiscal Q3 earnings are expected around Dec 1 (one secondary source).
invalidation: Exit if fiscal Q3 results or guidance around Dec 1 undercut the raised FY27/FY28 outlook, if the stock fails to hold above last week's post-deal low, or if deal terms or the regulatory timeline worsen further.

thesis: Apple's run to a record (new 52-week high at close) follows confirmed fiscal Q4 results: revenue of $114.5B, up 12% year over year, and EPS of $2.10. This suggests the earnings beat and the iPhone cycle, not just the post-midterm tech rally, are carrying the stock. On the other side, commentators point to a 'lack of momentum' and AI concerns, and the stock was dragged into the Nov 5 Nasdaq selloff, though it fell only about 1.5% against the index's 5.5%. A litigation event also sits inside the next 90 days: the Supreme Court has set oral argument in Apple v. Epic (the App Store contempt/link-out fee case) for Jan 11, 2027. Separately, the DOJ monopolization suit is in discovery through May 2027, with early settlement talks reported, and has no ruling scheduled soon.
invalidation: Revisit if the stock gives back the post-earnings breakout and closes back below the pre-earnings level, if Apple v. Epic goes badly for Apple in a way that threatens App Store fee economics, or if fiscal Q1 guidance or iPhone demand commentary weakens.

thesis: Oracle's 60-day slide reflects worry about how its AI buildout is financed. On Nov 2 it priced a roughly $20B raise: about 86.2M shares at $116 plus five note series with coupons of 7-8.65%, adding roughly $777M a year in interest, with total debt reported at about $108B. The reported $300B OpenAI agreement makes up a large share of the $664B backlog, so one customer's ability to pay is a concentration risk. Today's +8.8% move followed CoreWeave's funding update easing sector-wide AI debt fears, which suggests sentiment rather than Oracle-specific news. On the positive side, the raise matches Oracle's previously committed cap of $20B in additional AI financing through FY2030, which could limit further issuance, and Stephens upgraded the stock after investor day. A bondholder class action filed in Jan 2026 over 2025 bond-offering disclosures is still pending, with no hearing date found.
invalidation: Exit if Oracle seeks financing beyond the stated $20B cap, if OpenAI's payment capacity or contract terms deteriorate, or if fiscal Q2 FY27 results (expected mid-December, date not yet confirmed) show backlog conversion or cash flow falling short.

thesis: AMD's Q3 2026 report (Nov 3) showed revenue of ~$13.4B (+45% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $2.09, both above estimates; data center revenue nearly doubled to ~$8.55B as MI450 Helios racks began revenue shipments to Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle, and Q4 guidance was ~$17B +/-3%. This suggests the 60-day gain rests on a confirmed, company-specific beat-and-raise. Today's +7.3%, however, came in the broad CoreWeave-driven chip rally, and some coverage flagged a slightly lower margin guide, so not all of the recent move is company-specific; the stock also remains ~16% below its 52-week high after the October chip selloff. Litigation found includes the consolidated Ukrainian suits over chips allegedly diverted to Russia (no merits ruling or scheduled date found) and the Adeia ITC probe, terminated after settlement in April 2026; no governance events were found.
invalidation: Signs that MI450 ramp shipments are slipping, a Q4 revenue shortfall against the ~$17B guide, or a scheduled ruling in the export-diversion litigation

thesis: Dell's +11.8% session on 11-11 looks like a sector-wide bounce rather than a Dell-specific event: coverage ties it to CoreWeave's Q3 beat and raised outlook, which lifted AI-server names broadly (SMCI +8%, HPE +6%), after a roughly 45% drawdown from October 7 to November 5 that coincided with a post-midterm selloff. This suggests a relief rally in sentiment, not a newly disclosed change in Dell's own fundamentals. The fiscal Q3 report on November 24 is the next real company-specific data point and could confirm or reverse the read. The litigation check found only a January 2026 ERISA 401(k) class action with no scheduled ruling (the Class V suit settled in 2022), and no restatement, for-cause auditor change or executive indictment turned up in the last 3 years.
invalidation: Fiscal Q3 results on Nov 24 show AI-server orders/backlog and margins strong enough that the October-November drawdown looks fundamentally overdone, turning the rebound into a company-specific re-rating.

thesis: Tetra Tech fell about 7.5% intraday on 11-11 on 5x volume ahead of its results, with no company-specific reason given for the pre-report selling. After the close it reported fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS of $0.49 against a $0.47 consensus, record full-year EPS, backlog of $4.67B (+13% year over year) and $100M of Q4 buybacks, and after-hours trading (~$41.05) recovered the whole intraday drop. The strongest counter-evidence is that the FY27 revenue guide of $4.43-4.63B sits below FY26's $5.08B; even so, FY27 EPS guidance of $1.65-1.80 sits above FY26 adjusted EPS of $1.60, which suggests margin and mix improvement rather than deterioration. The $57M Hunters Point False Claims Act settlement (approved Aug 2026, no admission of liability) and the $1.5M residents' settlement are resolved; the developers' (Five Point/Lennar) suits are reportedly still moving toward trial with no scheduled date found, and the earlier Hunters Point employee guilty pleas predate the 3-year window.
invalidation: The Nov 12 call or analyst reaction treats the FY27 revenue decline as demand or contract loss (e.g., federal funding cuts), shares give back the after-hours recovery and close below the 11-11 intraday low (~$37.08), or a trial date is set in the Hunters Point developer litigation.

thesis: Resideo's +18% move follows its Q3 2026 report on 11-10, its first full quarter after the August 3 ADI spin-off: revenue of $727M against roughly $713M expected, adjusted EPS of $0.52 against roughly $0.34, a 14th straight quarter of gross margin expansion to 40.4%, and gross debt cut to $2.1B after $1.1B of repayment. This suggests the market is re-rating the standalone business after a weak year. The strongest counter-evidence is that Q4 revenue guidance ($710-730M) came in slightly below consensus and GAAP EPS fell 71% on $30M of separation costs; even so, the beat on underlying margin and deleveraging points the same way, and the separation costs are non-recurring. Spruce Point's January 2026 short report questioning acquisition accounting and CFO/CAO turnover, and a reported (date unconfirmed) handoff of the principal financial officer role from former CFO Michael Carlet to CEO Thomas Surran, could not be fully dismissed, though neither is a confirmed restatement. A Nebraska AG deceptive-practices suit exists, but no scheduled date in the next 90 days was found.
invalidation: An Item 4.02 non-reliance or restatement filing, confirmation that the CFO exit was tied to reporting problems, a scheduled ruling in the Nebraska AG case, or Q4 results missing the $710-730M guide.

thesis: Payoneer has a pending all-cash take-private by Nuvei (Advent) at $7.40 per share, signed June 2026; shareholders approved it on September 14, 2026 and the HSR waiting period ended early on July 28, while money-transmitter and non-U.S. payment-regulator approvals are still pending, with a targeted mid-2027 close and a June 12, 2027 outside date (plus an automatic 3-month extension). At ~$7.155 the stock trades about 3.4% under the deal price, which suggests the heavy volume and flat price are merger-arbitrage and positioning flows pinned to the deal spread, not new fundamental information. Upside is capped at $7.40, while downside if the deal breaks is large. Two merger lawsuits are pending, one seeking to block the deal, but no scheduled hearing date was found; no restatement, auditor change or executive indictment was found.
invalidation: Deal terms change (a higher bid or a price bump), or the merger is terminated or blocked, so the stock is no longer pinned to the $7.40 cash consideration.

thesis: First Advantage's drop to ~$21.55 on 11-10 coincides with Silver Lake's secondary sale of 15M shares, priced at $21.80 and closing around Nov 12; the company is not selling any shares and receives no proceeds. This followed a 12.5M-share Silver Lake sale in August. Fundamentals were strong just days earlier: Q3 revenue rose 13.8% to $465.8M (Nov 5), and the low end of the raised full-year guidance now exceeds the prior high end on every metric. This suggests the selloff is a sponsor-supply overhang rather than a fundamental deterioration, though up to 5.3M shares may be distributed to Silver Lake LPs outside the 30-day lock-up, so near-term overhang may persist. Litigation checks found only a plaintiff-firm investigation of a November 2025 data breach (no filed complaint or scheduled date in results) and older FCRA class actions; no restatement, auditor change or executive indictment was found.
invalidation: The 5.3M LP distribution and remaining Silver Lake stake keep pressing shares below the $21.80 offering price, or guidance is cut or a data-breach suit gets a scheduled court date, signaling the drop was not purely supply-driven.
